title: A Ghost for the Debt
premise: Cyrus Eastwick, a fixer for the Meridian Group—an embassy that exists on no map and answers to no flag—is ordered to extract Dr. Ilan Voss, a defector whose testimony could burn half her agency's network. But the flight manifest of Voss's inbound plane has been erased mid-air, and Cyrus realizes the extraction is theater: Voss is bait in an internal purge she was never meant to survive. Torn between duty to the institution that made her and loyalty to the one honest man in it, she runs the extraction anyway, trading her own identity for his. At dawn, the plane leaves with Voss aboard and Cyrus's records erased in turn—she becomes the ghost, finally free, finally belonging to no one but herself.
about_author: Rosalind Iversen is the pen name of a former diplomatic security consultant who spent a decade inside institutions that preferred not to be named. She writes thrillers about people who discover their loyalties were always negotiable.

chapters.title: The Rules Keep Changing
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. A routine document handoff at a Vienna café goes wrong when the dead-drop protocol changes without notice, nearly exposing her. She files a complaint that vanishes into the Meridian Group's bureaucracy. Emotional beat: unease—the machinery she serves is starting to misfire around her.

chapters.title: Manifest Zero
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Her handler, Adeyemi, summons her: Flight 4472 from Minsk landed—or didn't—and every record of it has been scrubbed while it was still airborne. Aboard was Dr. Ilan Voss, a defector carrying proof of Meridian's dirtiest operation. Emotional beat: cold dread dressed as professional calm.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Cyrus tracks Voss to a safehouse outside Bratislava using only paper trails the erasure missed. He's frightened, lucid, and insists he knows exactly why they wiped the flight: he's not being protected, he's being positioned. Emotional beat: first flicker of trust between strangers.

chapters.title: Dawn Is a Deadline
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. The extraction flight leaves at dawn from a disused airstrip; Adeyemi gives her twelve hours and a clean gun. Cyrus notices the exfil route passes through territory controlled by the faction that wants Voss silenced. Emotional beat: the arithmetic of betrayal begins.

chapters.title: What the Institution Owes
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus, flashback-heavy. Seven years ago Meridian rebuilt her after a scandal destroyed her old life—new name, new history, total dependence. She remembers signing away her past and wonders what else she signed away. Emotional beat: grief for the woman she used to be.

chapters.title: A Quiet Room in Bratislava
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. In his own voice for the first time: Voss explains what he found—a ledger proving Meridian sold out its own assets to buy peace with a rival service. He chose defection knowing he'd be bait. Emotional beat: moral clarity that makes Cyrus's gray world look worse.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. She preps the extraction while running quiet checks on Adeyemi and finds his comms pattern changed three days before the flight vanished—he knew. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Second Fixer
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. A rival fixer, Kestrel, appears at her hotel—same training, same blank file, sent to shadow the job. They share drinks and mutual recognition: one of them won't see dawn. Emotional beat: kinship between two instruments who know they're expendable.

chapters.title: Ledger of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. Voss shows Cyrus the ledger's key page: her own recruitment was part of a trade—she was handed to Meridian as collateral years ago. Her entire career was someone else's payment. Emotional beat: identity shattered and reassembled as anger.

chapters.title: Call It Duty
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Adeyemi calls with new orders: deliver Voss to a secondary site, not the airstrip. The orders contradict everything. Cyrus says yes, then begins planning the real extraction behind a wall of perfect compliance. Emotional beat: love against duty—she chooses the man over the machine.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Offer
chapters.summary: POV: Kestrel. Kestrel reveals she was sent to kill Voss if Cyrus wavered, and offers Cyrus a way out: walk away, let her do the job, keep her clean record. Cyrus refuses. Emotional beat: two women acknowledging the cage before one of them breaks it.

chapters.title: Paper Trail
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Cyrus burns her own contingency caches, forging a false trail suggesting Voss fled west alone. Every move costs her another piece of her cover. Emotional beat: exhilaration and terror of becoming unmade on purpose.

chapters.title: The Purge List
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. Voss decrypts more of the ledger: the flight erasure was the opening move of an internal purge, and Cyrus's name is on the second list. The extraction was designed to fail with her attached. Emotional beat: horror converting to purpose.

chapters.title: Night Moves
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. The run to the airstrip through fog and checkpoints, dodging both Meridian's hunters and the rival service's. Kestrel appears again—not to stop them, but to slow the hunters down, paying a debt of her own. Emotional beat: unexpected grace in a ruthless night.

chapters.title: What Adeyemi Wanted
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Confrontation with Adeyemi at the airstrip fence: he confesses he rewrote her orders hoping she'd defy them and die clean, sparing himself the choice. She leaves him alive with the truth. Emotional beat: pity for a man who never stopped obeying.

chapters.title: Runway Lights
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. The plane is late; hunters close in; Voss offers to surrender so she can survive. She refuses—his testimony matters more than her record. The engines appear out of the dark. Emotional beat: love expressed as refusal to let go.

chapters.title: The Choice at Dawn
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Climax: boarding under fire, Kestrel wounded covering them, Cyrus realizes there's room for one passenger story to survive—hers or Voss's, not both. She hands the ledger to Voss, keeps the gun, and stays on the ground as the wheels lift. Emotional beat: sacrifice as self-authorship.

chapters.title: Erased
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Meridian wipes her file within hours—name, history, seven years gone. She walks out of Vienna as a ghost with cash, a false passport, and nothing owed. Emotional beat: terrifying freedom.

chapters.title: The Woman Without a File
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Weeks later, hiding in Porto, Cyrus learns the purge consumed Adeyemi and half the directorate; Voss's testimony detonated in three capitals. She reads her own obituary in a trade journal. Emotional beat: vindication laced with mourning.

chapters.title: Signals
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. An encrypted message arrives—Voss, alive, safe, asking nothing except whether she's free. She replies with a single word. Emotional beat: tenderness across distance, belonging chosen rather than assigned.

chapters.title: A Ghost for the Debt
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Kestrel surfaces in Porto, healed, unemployed, and proposes they work the margins together—fixers without a master. Cyrus hesitates, then signs a partnership instead of a contract. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt on equal terms.

chapters.title: No One's Instrument
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Final scene: a new client, a new job, rules she writes herself. On the airstrip where she once gave everything away, Cyrus watches a plane take off and feels nothing but ownership of her own name—even if it isn't hers. Emotional beat: resolution—identity as something made, not given.
